A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Evaluating Large Language Models for Detecting Antisemitism. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across eight LLMs, Guided-CoT ablations, statistical analyses of generated explanations and manual analysis of misclassified posts.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including classification scores, explanation analyses and the 260-post misclassification study.

M1.justification: The five-step Guided-CoT prompt, inputs, outputs and inference procedures are unchanged, including Figure 19. Section 5.1 clarifies the existing median-distance and PCA analysis without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same IHRA-labeled English Twitter dataset and its earlier release for the GPT-3.5 comparison. No dataset, domain, language or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The model and comparator membership within experiments remains unchanged: the same zero-shot variants, Zero-Shot-CoT and cited fine-tuned GPT-3.5 comparison are retained.

E3.justification: Evaluation subsets, decoding settings, classification metrics and embedding/UMAP/PCA procedures remain unchanged. The revised equations in Section 5.1 describe existing computations rather than a different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The five leave-one-thought-out ablations, response-behavior and explanation analyses, and 260-post error study are retained unchanged. The appendices add no new sensitivity tests or case studies.

E5.justification: Five sampling repetitions, 30-inference self-consistency, sampling 1,500 responses per class for significance analysis, and the KS tests and significance notation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings match throughout, including the appendices. For example, Table 4 retains Guided-CoT F1 scores of 0.72 and 0.73 versus the cited GPT-3.5 score of 0.70, and Table 5 retains the same divergence values.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 corrects Equation (3)'s undefined f_A summand to the defined SDV_A, repairing the formal SCMD definition. The added PCA equation (4) restates the previously described projection rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The expanded abstract explicitly mentions domain-specific guidance and refusal reduction, but these contributions were already claimed in v1's introduction and body. The central claims and their scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model divergence, stylistic regularization and misclassification remain unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning English Twitter data, policy coverage, hyperparameters and comparisons using different subsets.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, quantization details, decoding parameters, complete prompt templates and code/resource access information are unchanged. The additional notation explanation does not disclose new implementation settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited-work set and positioning relative to earlier antisemitism detection and prompting research are unchanged. Reference reflow does not add or remove sources.

P1.justification: v2 expands the abstract and locally rewrites Section 5.1 to explain embedding notation and introduce question-style ranking and clustering subheadings. Minor punctuation and cross-reference edits accompany these changes; the overall organization is retained.

P2.justification: Equation displays in Section 5.1 are rearranged and expanded, and surrounding text reflows; Section 5.2 begins on page 8 instead of page 7. Figures and tables retain their content and design, including all appendix displays.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and mathematical precision by repairing the undefined summand in Equation (3) and explaining the ranking and clustering analysis more explicitly. The abstract also better communicates existing findings. The empirical evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
